name: Bite reclamation

lead: Bite reclamation reopens a bite that has collapsed from tooth wear, such as from grinding or acid reflux, restoring the height of the lower face. Worn teeth can leave the lower face looking shortened, with the chin close to the nose.

Worn teeth are rebuilt so the jaws meet at a greater vertical dimension. It is described as part of complex full-mouth reconstruction involving many teeth; only brief encyclopedic descriptions were found, with no trials.

paras: It is large restorative dental work covering many teeth, usually planned and staged by a dentist. Temporaries or previews are often used to check appearance and bite.
Sources describe the work as complex, and no safety data specific to the procedure were found.

chain: Longer teeth and fuller lower face
angle.text: Those with teeth worn down by grinding or acid use bite reclamation to rebuild height, which can make the lower face look less shortened. Teeth are restored so the jaws meet higher, as part of full-mouth reconstruction.

lead: Bite reclamation is a term used in cosmetic dentistry for reopening the bite to restore vertical dimension lost through wear, such as from grinding or acid reflux, which can make the lower face look shortened.[1] It is described as part of full-mouth reconstruction, complex work involving many teeth.[1]

The looks payoff is the lower third of the face and the teeth themselves. Vertical dimension of occlusion is the up-and-down relationship of the jaws when the teeth meet, and dental references describe a deficient vertical dimension as giving a collapsed look with the chin close to the nose.[2] Rebuilding worn teeth to a greater height restores tooth length and lower-face height, which is why the procedure appears in hardmaxxing discussions of jaw and smile aesthetics.

Tooth wear has several causes, including attrition from grinding or clenching and erosion from acid, and wear can alter the occlusal vertical dimension.[3] A long-term study of severely worn dentitions rebuilt with direct composite at an increased vertical dimension followed patients for up to 11 years.[4]
infobox: Tooth wear from grinding or acid

paras: Cosmetic dentistry sources describe worn teeth reducing vertical dimension and bite reclamation restoring it.[1] Vertical dimension is assessed by facial proportion, speech sounds and rest position.[2]

Tooth wear is loss of tooth substance from causes other than decay and is usually multifactorial. Attrition comes from tooth-to-tooth contact and habits such as bruxism; erosion comes from acid in foods, drinks or reflux conditions such as GERD.[3] Severe wear can reduce tooth height and destabilise the bite, and the occlusal vertical dimension may change as a result.[3]

Dental references describe first identifying and controlling the cause, applying preventive measures and reviewing the patient for six to twelve months before restoration is considered.[3] Options for restoring lost height include increasing the vertical dimension, occlusal adjustment, crown lengthening or orthodontic extrusion, and the Dahl approach, in which the bite is propped open so worn teeth extrude.[3]

A 2021 clinical study followed 13 patients with severely worn dentitions whose 164 teeth were rebuilt with direct microhybrid or nanofilled composite at an increased vertical dimension of occlusion. After a mean of 10.7 years (first cohort) or 5.2 years (second cohort), overall restoration quality was good, nanofilled composite showed less surface degradation and better margins, and the authors recorded repairs and replacements of some restorations.[4]
